chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the person who is unconscious (fainted). He said, then he said: 'He must make up the prayer of that day.'

key_terms.اَلْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ: The person who is unconscious or has fainted
key_terms.يَقْضِي: He makes up (performs the missed obligatory act)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up prayers after fainting or losing consciousness?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the specific ruling for a person who faints (mughama 'alayh) is clarified: they are required to perform the makeup (qada) of the obligatory prayers missed during the period of unconsciousness. This ruling, found in the chapter of the 'Compelled One' (al-Mudtirri), highlights the Shia juristic view that the loss of consciousness does not exempt one from the duty of prayer, but rather suspends it until recovery, at which point the missed units must be fulfilled.
